title: The Royal Rivalry, Episode 2: The Storm Arrives (full episode)
series: The Royal Rivalry (Clash of Clans fan comic), full episodes

lines: Previously, on The Royal Rivalry. Two heroes. One statue. And one very bad night.
The Barbarian King and the Archer Queen were given one job: guard the gold. Together.
They guarded each other instead. Twenty goblins walked away rich.
But on a storm-dark hill beyond the walls, something had watched the whole thing.
The morning after the raid, the Grand Warden called both heroes to the broken wall.
You lost the gold together. So together, you will rebuild this wall.
The King carried three stones at once, because carrying one stone was for people with small arms.
The Queen placed each stone with a ruler, because a wall should be straight. Obviously.
It's a wall, not a painting.
By noon, they had drawn a line right down the middle of the wall.
It's... one wall. You do know it's one wall?
The villagers took sides again, of course.
Team King snack delivery! Extra crunchy!
Tea for the Queen. Exactly as you like it.
Is that tea? Can I have some tea?
Then a letter arrived, nailed to an arrow, signed with a muddy green thumbprint.
Dear King and Queen. Thank you for the gold. Same time next week? Love, the Goblins.
I will hunt down every goblin in this valley.
You couldn't hunt down one. I was there.
In the Town Hall, the Wizard gave his daily weather report.
Clear skies all week. Not a single cloud. Lovely weather for wall building.
High above the hills, a cloud disagreed.
That afternoon, a visitor flew in over the walls. The kingdom's Healer, back from a long journey.
Is it just me, or is the wind strange today? It makes my wings tingle.
You have felt this wind before, haven't you?
Once. Many years ago, before there were walls here. Before there was a kingdom.
Ask me again tomorrow. If there is a tomorrow.
Down by the collectors, the Elixir began to do something it had never done before.
The Elixir is... fizzing. Elixir does not fizz. Why is it fizzing?
Every drop of it was trembling, and every drop was pointing at the hills.
Beyond the walls, the Goblin Boss sniffed the wind, and turned very pale. Very pale, for a green person.
Boys. Pack up the snacks. We're leaving.
But we just unpacked the snacks!
When goblins run away from something, everybody else should too.
That night, the Warden sat alone with his Eternal Tome, the old book that had shielded this kingdom a hundred times.
Its pages turned by themselves, and stopped on a drawing of a storm.
I have felt this wind before. Long ago. I had hoped never to feel it again.
The next day, at noon, the sky went dark. No rain. No wind. Just a low, crackling hum.
Uh, is it supposed to be night at lunchtime?
Then a single bolt of lightning struck the new wall. Exactly on the line down the middle.
It hit the line. The line is mine.
Both of you. Quiet. Look up.
Out of the clouds came a shape. Long wings. Glowing blue scales. And a mouth full of lightning.
An Electro Dragon. The biggest anyone had ever seen.
DRAGON! Big one! Very sparkly! Everybody panic!
Wizard, don't tell them to panic!
The kingdom's towers fired. The Air Defense launched its rockets. The Archer Towers let their arrows fly.
The dragon opened its mouth, and the lightning jumped. From tower, to tower, to tower.
The Barbarians threw their swords at the dragon. The swords went up. The swords came back down.
Everyone stand back. This dragon is MINE.
You can't punch something that flies.
The King ran. The King jumped. The King jumped higher than any King had ever jumped.
He missed the dragon by about forty feet, and landed in the fountain.
Still counting that as a fountain win, by the way.
Out of my way. A dragon is just a very large target.
She fired. Ten arrows in two seconds. Every one of them hit.
Every one of them bounced off the crackling scales, and fell to the ground, melted.
The King climbed out of the fountain, grabbed a barrel, and threw it at the dragon with all his might.
The barrel flew beautifully. Straight past the dragon. Straight into the Queen's crossbow.
You were standing where I was throwing!
She fixed her aim, and fired again. The arrow meant for the dragon struck the King's helmet instead.
Your head was in my shot.
Your shot was in my HEAD!
The Barbarians charged to help their King. The Archers rushed to help their Queen.
They met in the middle of the square, in one big, tight, shoving crowd.
One bolt struck the first Barbarian, jumped to an Archer, then another, then twelve more.
The Healer dove into the smoke, her wings glowing gold, and one by one, the soldiers got back up.
Spread out! Lightning jumps between you when you stand too close!
Half the soldiers ran left. Half ran right. A few ran in a small, confused circle.
I'll just... follow the dragon, then?
STOP! Both of you! Together, or not at all!
But the King and Queen were far too busy shouting at each other to hear him.
The dragon turned its head toward the Town Hall. Toward the Elixir storage. Toward the heart of the kingdom.
Between the dragon and the Town Hall stood one old man.
The Grand Warden opened his Eternal Tome.
Golden light poured out of its pages, and spread over the village like a great glowing dome.
The dragon breathed the biggest bolt of lightning the kingdom had ever seen.
It struck the golden shield. And the shield held.
NOW! Strike it together while it's tired! King, the jump! Queen, the shot!
It was the perfect chance. The dragon hung there, gasping, just above the shield.
The King jumped for the dragon. The Queen fired at the dragon. From opposite sides. At the very same moment.
His jump carried him straight into the path of her arrow. Again.
Both heroes crashed to the ground. And the dragon, rested now, breathed again.
For eight long seconds, the golden shield held.
Then it cracked. Then it shattered.
And the lightning found the one person standing in its way.
The dragon circled once over the silent village. Then it rose into the clouds, and was gone.
Behind it, burned into the sky, it left a strange mark.
Then, finally, it began to rain.
The King and Queen ran to the Warden. Neither one of them ran faster than the other this time.
Old man? Hey. Wake up. You're supposed to be yelling at us right now.
Warden. Please. Please open your eyes.
The Warden's eyes opened, just a little.
Two halves... of one hero. Remember?
The Healer landed beside him, and her hands glowed gold.
He's breathing. Barely. I need the whole night, and I need quiet.
Which means the two of you need to stop shouting. For once.
The villagers gathered in the rain. Nobody cheered for Team King. Nobody cheered for Team Queen.
If you had hit the dragon instead of my helmet...
If you had stayed out of my shot...
And for the first time in their lives, neither of them finished the argument.
Later that night, the King stood alone at the wall. At the line down the middle.
He looked at it for a long time. Then he rubbed it out with his boot.
On the archery range, the Queen saw him do it. She didn't say a word.
But she quietly put down her ruler.
All night long, the Healer worked. And all night long, two heroes sat on the bench outside her door.
The same bench. At opposite ends. But the same bench.
Do you think he'll wake up?
He has to. Who else is going to yell at us?
And in the Town Hall, the Eternal Tome lay on the Warden's table. Its pages turned once more, all by themselves.
They stopped on the drawing of the storm. Beside it, someone had written a single word: Titan.
Because that dragon did not come on its own. Someone sent it.
Someone with the power of a storm. And they were not finished.
To be continued. Should the King and Queen finally team up? Tell me in the comments.
